title: Starting System Specifications — 2.3L EcoBoost
introduction:
I read these specifications as effort and result: current draw describes the starter’s electrical demand, while cranking speed describes how quickly the engine turns. Match the measurement to the correct row and its printed units. No-load, normal-load and maximum-load current figures describe different conditions; the maximum is not a target to chase.

Keep every qualifier with its value. The cranking-speed, no-load-current and normal-load-current rows are marked as averages. The starting-circuit voltage-drop row is also marked as an average and specifies an engine at normal operating temperature. Voltage drop is voltage used across part of a circuit while current flows; excessive drop can reveal resistance that a no-load check misses.

This table supplies comparison figures, not equipment connections, measurement timing or fault-isolation branches. Use the matching engine diagnostic instructions to obtain and interpret measurements; a number on this page alone is no verdict on the starter.

edits.why: The row conditions determine which comparisons are meaningful. Retain the average labels and the temperature condition, and distinguish normal current demand from the maximum-load specification.
